meta.provenance_note: Read directly from the PDF via PyMuPDF on 2026-09-18 — extraction is clean (this book is in English). Unit titles, page numbers, vocabulary, grammar structures, and listening skill descriptors were taken from the book's own two-page 'Scope and sequence' table (pp. 4-5), same source and treatment as g4EnglishSem1.ts/g5EnglishSem1.ts. Only the Vocabulary/Grammar/Listening columns of that table were used, matching the established precedent; the Speaking/Reading/Writing/Project/Viewing columns on page 5 were not used. Each numbered unit is split into two lessons — Vocabulary & Grammar, and Listening & Speaking — reflecting the two content halves the table itself separates.
known_gaps: This is real content (vocabulary lists, grammar phrases, listening skill descriptors), not title-only — but it is unit-level, not lesson-level: each unit's actual internal lesson count and exact per-page lesson titles were not verified page by page.

Following the g4/g5 English precedent, `main_idea_ar` and `objectives` hold literal English text (this book's own language), not Arabic; `title_ar` carries a plain Arabic gloss of the English title for search/display.

Phonics letter/word-family lists printed inside the table's Vocabulary column (e.g. Unit 1: 's, d, c, a' / 'sing, sister, six, sun, dig, dad, doll, duck, ...') are excluded from `vocabulary` — they are letter-sound drill items, not thematic vocabulary, and this schema has no separate field for them.

The book's own 'Welcome: Hello!' section is unnumbered in the table of contents (units are numbered 1-4 starting at 'Family and friends') — modeled here as an unnumbered unit (`number: 0`), the same technique used for the prep unit in iqra_curriculum_g1_math_sem1.json. Unlike Semester 2's own Welcome unit, this one has no Grammar or Listening entry in the scope-and-sequence table — only a unit-objectives sentence and a vocabulary list (numbers, colours) — so it carries a single 'Vocabulary' lesson rather than the two-lesson shape used everywhere else; no content was invented to fill a second lesson.
